scholarships.title: SA-TIED Request for Research Proposals: Public revenue mobilization; Poverty, inequality, and labour markets
scholarships.official_source: United Nations University World Institute for Development Economics Research (UNU-WIDER), with the National Treasury of South Africa

existing.description: UNU-WIDER and the South African National Treasury invite proposals under the third phase of the Southern Africa - Towards Inclusive Economic Development (SA-TIED) programme for research using South African tax administrative data. Accepted proposals are paid a research honorarium in the range of US$3,000-10,000 on delivery of a working paper of 10,000 words or fewer, and the resulting papers are published in the SA-TIED research paper series. This is research funding rather than a degree scholarship: the deliverable is a policy paper, and the honorarium is expected to cover all expenses of the research.
eligibility: Proposals from individuals, groups of individuals, and non-profit organizations are welcome
Calls for South Africa-based and international researchers to submit proposals
Research must be conducted primarily, but not exclusively, using South African tax administrative data
Papers must be written in English and limited to 10,000 words or fewer, inclusive of text, tables, figures, footnotes and references
Papers may use either theoretical or empirical approaches
Researchers requiring access to National Treasury tax administrative datasets will be subject to agreed restrictions to preserve confidentiality
existing.eligibility_summary: Proposals are welcome from individuals, groups of individuals and non-profit organisations, using South Africa-based and international researchers, with South African researchers, women, and early-career and Global South scholars particularly encouraged.
benefits: Publication of the resulting paper under UNU-WIDER copyright as an SA-TIED research paper
Possible publication in the WIDER Working Paper Series
Opportunity to participate in at least one knowledge-sharing event
Engagement with the SA-TIED communications team to develop a knowledge mobilization output such as a video, social media product, infographic, brief or blog
Inclusion in a research team building capacity in South African institutions, with UNU-WIDER seeking participation from Historically Disadvantaged Institutions
coverage: Research honorarium in the range of US$3,000-10,000, paid upon delivery of a working paper depending on the qualifications of the lead researcher and assessment of the proposal
A small travel stipend for researchers using the South African tax administrative data who live outside of Gauteng
requirements: Proposals must be submitted electronically using the online form on the RfRP announcement page
Three forms are provided: one for individuals, one for groups of individuals, and one for non-profit organizations
Details such as address, gender, nationality and date of birth of all researchers involved must be entered on the form
The cover page, the proposal, and short CVs of five pages or less per researcher must be uploaded
The provided proposal template must be used for the proposal
documents: Short CV of five pages or less for each researcher involved
Details of all researchers involved: address, gender, nationality and date of birth
existing.english_requirement: Working papers need to be written in English
application_method: Download the Request for Research Proposals document and the proposal template
Prepare the proposal using the provided template, observing the word limits
Select the correct online form: individual, group of individuals, or non-profit organization
Enter the contact details and the details of all researchers involved, including address, gender, nationality and date of birth
Upload the cover page, the proposal and short CVs of five pages or less per researcher
Submit the form before 15 October 2026 at 23:59 UTC+2
Send any questions on the proposal process to researchproposal3@wider.unu.edu by 8 October 2026
For successful proposals, sign a consultant contract or institutional contractual agreement with UNU-WIDER
existing.selection_notes: Each proposal is reviewed for scientific merit and feasibility and selected on three criteria: relevance to the research project, strength of empirical and policy contributions, and qualifications and experience of the research team. Preference is given to applications from early-career and female scholars and researchers from South Africa. Only the final decision on whether the proposal is accepted is communicated; applicants must not expect feedback on their proposals. Funding decisions are targeted for 9 November 2026.
existing.best_fit: Qualified individual researchers, groups and non-profit organisations able to conduct high-quality economic research on public revenue mobilization, poverty, inequality and labour markets, using South African tax administrative data. Applications from women and South African researchers are particularly encouraged, and preference is given to early-career researchers and scholars from the Global South.
existing.notes: Successful researchers or their institutions sign a consultant contract or institutional contractual agreement with UNU-WIDER under UNU conditions of service, and transfer copyright of the research produced to UNU-WIDER so that it can be licensed on full open access; if no further publication is expected, copyright can be transferred back to the authors. Any material published externally thereafter should carry due acknowledgement of UNU-WIDER as the original commissioning institute. Successful applicants may be asked to attend at least one knowledge-sharing event and a work-in-progress workshop of about 1-1.5 days.
existing.duration: Milestone-driven: first draft of papers due 8 June 2027 and final draft due 8 September 2027, with a work-in-progress workshop in June or July 2027
existing.application_period: Launched 17 September 2026; proposals close 15 October 2026 at 23:59 UTC+2. Questions on the proposal process were due by 8 October 2026, with queries and responses published on the RfRP announcement page and updated on a rolling basis.
existing.deadline_display: Closing date: 15 October 2026, 23:59 (UTC+2). Submit questions by 8 October 2026.
